name: 3D Design Combination System
purpose: Provide a large but controlled library of concrete 3D design directions without allowing visually impressive but semantically unrelated scenes.
selectionRule: First choose a scene archetype whose domain and page purpose match verified business facts. Then choose an art-direction treatment that fits the brand, content and capability tier. The semantic relevance contract remains mandatory and may reject a mathematically possible combination.
hardRules: Do not select by visual novelty alone.
The scene subject, environment, props, materials, lighting, motion and fallback must all fit the business and page purpose.
A domain mismatch is rejected even when the composition or treatment is attractive.
Primary visual subjects require semantic relevance score 4 or 5; secondary decoration requires at least 3.
When a real product, property, venue or facility is represented, use verified geometry/media or clearly label conceptual visualisation internally.
Choose the smallest sufficient medium before defaulting to full WebGL/WebGPU.

sceneArchetypes.name: Hero Object Pedestal
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Give one verified product or object a controlled inspection-focused hero stage.

sceneArchetypes.name: Exploded Product Stack
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Explain the verified components or construction of a product.

sceneArchetypes.name: Cutaway Section
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Reveal internal structure that materially improves understanding.

sceneArchetypes.name: Macro Material Inspection
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Show texture, finish, fabric, surface or verified material quality at close range.

sceneArchetypes.name: Turntable Product View
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Allow a simple 360-degree inspection of a verified product.

sceneArchetypes.name: Configurable Swatch Stage
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Preview verified colours, finishes or materials while keeping configuration controls in the DOM.

sceneArchetypes.name: Packaging & Unbox Sequence
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Explain packaging, delivery presentation or product contents when those details matter.

sceneArchetypes.name: Assembly Process
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Demonstrate a verified build, installation or assembly process.

sceneArchetypes.name: Ingredient or Component Orbit
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Show verified ingredients, components or contributing elements around the central subject.

sceneArchetypes.name: Spatial Timeline
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Turn a verified chronological story or process into a spatial journey without losing semantic reading order.

sceneArchetypes.name: Room Walkthrough
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Let users understand a verified room, venue, exhibit or interior spatially.

sceneArchetypes.name: Building Massing
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Explain building form, blocks, orientation or development stages.

sceneArchetypes.name: Floorplan Extrusion
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Convert a verified plan into an understandable 3D spatial overview.

sceneArchetypes.name: Isometric Process Map
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Explain a service, operational or fulfilment process with spatial grouping.

sceneArchetypes.name: Logistics Route Network
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Show verified routes, hubs, flows or service coverage.

sceneArchetypes.name: Globe Network
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Visualise genuinely global locations, clients, infrastructure or flows.

sceneArchetypes.name: Data Constellation
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Represent verified relationships, clusters or network data spatially.

sceneArchetypes.name: Layered System Architecture
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Explain verified technical, organisational or service layers.

sceneArchetypes.name: Document-to-Data Morph
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Visualise a real transformation from documents or inputs into structured information.

sceneArchetypes.name: Typography Sculpture
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use a verified name, phrase, monogram or key concept as a spatial display element while keeping readable DOM text.

sceneArchetypes.name: Portal Gallery
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use portals to organise real collections, destinations, memories or projects.

sceneArchetypes.name: Floating Card World
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Arrange semantic content cards in a restrained spatial field without making the canvas the only navigation method.

sceneArchetypes.name: Character Guide
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use a brand-appropriate guide to explain steps, onboarding or a story when a character genuinely helps comprehension.

sceneArchetypes.name: Low-Poly Campus or World
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Create a simplified navigable representation of a verified campus, venue, destination or learning world.

sceneArchetypes.name: Museum Exhibit Stage
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Present a real artefact, memory object or educational exhibit with annotations.

sceneArchetypes.name: Event Monogram Scene
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Build a restrained spatial identity moment around the verified couple/event monogram.

sceneArchetypes.name: Ceremonial Object Composition
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use verified rings, flowers, fabric, invitation materials or venue motifs as a culturally appropriate celebration composition.

sceneArchetypes.name: Nature & Organic Field
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use verified botanical, ingredient, environmental or natural forms as atmosphere tied to the offering.

sceneArchetypes.name: Liquid Brand Metaphor
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Use fluid motion only when liquid, formulation, flow or transformation has a defensible connection to the product or service.

sceneArchetypes.name: AR Placement Preview
sceneArchetypes.purpose: Let users preview a verified object at scale in their environment when placement materially improves confidence.

artDirections.name: Studio Neutral
artDirections.bestWhen: The object itself should dominate and colour accuracy matters.

artDirections.name: Dark Cinematic
artDirections.bestWhen: A verified product or story benefits from dramatic reveal.
artDirections.avoid: Hiding practical information or using darkness as a generic premium shortcut.

artDirections.name: Editorial Light
artDirections.bestWhen: Content, typography and 3D must share equal importance.

artDirections.name: Translucent Glass
artDirections.bestWhen: Glass, transparency, layering or formulation is materially relevant.
artDirections.avoid: Applying glass effects to unrelated industries merely because they look futuristic.

artDirections.name: Clay Matte
artDirections.bestWhen: A simplified explanatory or approachable tone is appropriate.
artDirections.avoid: Misrepresenting premium material finishes that users need to inspect accurately.

artDirections.name: Metallic Precision
artDirections.bestWhen: Engineering, hardware, automotive or metal products are genuinely involved.
artDirections.avoid: Random chrome treatment for food, weddings or soft-service brands.

artDirections.name: Soft Gradient World
artDirections.bestWhen: An abstract environment supports a verified brand concept without pretending to show a real place.
artDirections.avoid: Replacing meaningful product imagery with vague gradients.

artDirections.name: Blueprint Technical
artDirections.bestWhen: Dimensions, architecture, engineering, process or verified systems are central.

artDirections.name: Warm Material
traits: wood, paper, fabric or warm stone
artDirections.bestWhen: Hospitality, food, celebration, interiors or tactile consumer products support the treatment.
artDirections.avoid: Applying warm material props that contradict the actual venue/product.

artDirections.name: Monochrome Sculptural
artDirections.bestWhen: Shape and structure matter more than surface colour.
artDirections.avoid: Using monochrome when real product colour is an important decision factor.
